memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Moses and the elders of Israel returned to the camp. Now a wind went out from the Lord and drove quail in from the sea. It scattered them up to two cubits deep all around the camp, as far as a day's walk in any direction. All that day and night and all the next day the people went out and gathered quail. No one gathered less than ten homers. Then they spread them out all around the camp. — Num 11:30-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God said He would provide meat, and He did — abundantly, overwhelmingly. Quail came in on the wind and lay heaped around the camp. What Moses had thought impossible, God accomplished with a single wind from the sea. "Is the Lord's arm too short?" Clearly not.

There is a lesson here in God's faithfulness to His word — even when His word is a warning. God had promised meat until they loathed it, and the quail arrived in staggering quantity. What God says, He does. His promises and His warnings are equally sure.

But look closely at the people's response. They gathered frantically, day and night and into the next day, hoarding far more than they could ever need. Their craving had not been satisfied; it had only grown greedier. Given abundance, they grasped for more rather than pausing in gratitude.

This is a warning for our own hearts. Getting what we crave rarely cures the craving; more often it feeds it. True contentment is never found in the size of the pile we gather. It is found in the God who provides. As Jesus taught, life does not consist in the abundance of our possessions. Better to gather little with a grateful heart than mountains with a greedy one.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When God provides, do you respond with gratitude or grasp for more?
2. Where might greed be disguising itself as need in your life?
3. How can you cultivate contentment in what God has already given?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are faithful to every word You speak. Guard my heart from greed, and teach me contentment and gratitude in Your provision. Let me trust You rather than my own gathering. Amen.
